A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAPO-CoT study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite additions, relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 6, Figures 2–4 and Appendix C report original GPT-5.2 and Gemini 2.5 Pro experiments on MAJORITY, MATCH3 and REACHABILITY.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds GPT-5.2 results on MAX, RIGHTMOSTEVEN and EQUALITY in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Theorem 5.10 and Appendix D add a pointer-chasing cBAPO-CoT procedure that outputs successive function iterates using one token per iteration. The BAPO/cBAPO framework and the original three task-solving constructions remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluated MAX, RIGHTMOSTEVEN and EQUALITY tasks, extending coverage from the three BAPO-hard problems to a contrasting class of BAPO-easy problems. Pointer chasing is a theoretical addition, not an evaluated task.

E2.justification: The retained experiments compare the same models, reasoning levels and prompting approaches. Figure 5 extends existing GPT-5.2 reasoning-level comparisons to new tasks; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The retained experiments keep the same input-size grid, 250 positive plus 250 negative instances, model settings and 50/100/200-word constraints. Figure 5 uses the existing reasoning-effort sweep and accuracy/token measures. Its task-specific sampling and prompts are not supplied, so no further protocol change is established.

E4.justification: Section 6.1 and Figure 5 add an analysis contrasting token scaling on BAPO-easy and BAPO-hard tasks. The existing budget experiments, decomposition analysis and example-CoT case studies in Sections 6.2–6.3 and Tables 2–4 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: There is no added seed or repeated-run information, significance testing, or changed uncertainty-estimation procedure. The retained plots preserve their uncertainty displays, and Figure 5 follows the existing reporting style.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds a distinct empirical scaling pattern: MAX and EQUALITY achieve high accuracy with low or plateauing reasoning-token usage, especially at lower reasoning efforts, while RIGHTMOSTEVEN retains increasing but much lower usage. The plotted data in Figures 2–4 and example outputs in Tables 2–4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 5.9, Theorem 5.10 and Appendix D introduce pointer-chasing definitions, constructions and hardness proofs addressing sublinear token complexity. Proposition 5.4 also corrects prefix parsing when no padding symbol occurs. The new Theorem D.2 has an internal mismatch: its statement requires κ ≥ 2ℓb + 3, but its proof later assumes κ ≥ 2ℓb + 5.

C1.justification: v1 leaves the existence of BAPO-hard problems with sublinear token complexity open. v2's introduction explicitly claims pointer chasing supplies such examples, adding a qualitatively new theoretical contribution while retaining the original three-task claims.

C2.justification: Figure 5 attributes easy-task efficiency to transformer parallelism and suggests imperfect positional encoding explains RIGHTMOSTEVEN's residual token growth, contrasting this with BAPO's exact index access. Section 8 also sharpens the remaining REACHABILITY question to O(m+n) versus Θ(n²); the existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link for reproducing experiments and identifies API fields used to obtain internal reasoning-token counts. Existing model/API versions, generation procedures and prompts are retained. The supplied PDFs do not establish the linked repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: Section 7 substantially broadens positioning through connections to Abbe et al.'s globality barrier, Kim et al.'s Markov-chain perspective, additional expressivity bounds, conflicting empirical length–accuracy findings, and compression/adaptive-stopping research. Appendix D additionally connects pointer chasing to classical communication complexity.

P1.justification: A substantial new explanatory appendix introduces BAPO through a detailed walkthrough and PARITY, INDEX and EQUALITY examples. Proofs of Propositions 4.4, 5.3 and 5.4 move from the appendix into the main text. These changes make the exposition more self-contained, alongside localized introductory edits and expanded related work.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5, places Figures 2 and 3 on separate pages, and places Tables 2 and 3 together. Table 1 becomes narrower through abbreviated theorem references, and Figure 3's panel titles change capitalization. Existing diagrams, plotted data and table contents are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The BAPO primer improves accessibility, and the easy-task comparisons provide useful empirical context beyond v1's hard-task experiments. Code-access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are qualified by incomplete protocols for Figure 5 and inconsistencies in the new pointer-chasing hardness proof, including Theorem D.2's threshold mismatch, so the overall improvement is limited.
